symptoms: Check engine light, rough idle, reduced fuel efficiency
likely_causes: Vacuum leak, dirty mass airflow sensor, weak fuel pump
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for code P0171. 2. Inspect vacuum hoses for cracks. 3. Clean MAF sensor. 4. Measure fuel pressure. 5. Verify O2 sensor operation.

symptoms: Check engine light, engine vibration, loss of power
likely_causes: Worn spark plugs, faulty ignition coils, low fuel pressure
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P0300 code. 2. Perform spark plug inspection/replacement. 3. Test ignition coils with a coil tester. 4. Check fuel pressure with gauge. 5. Scan for additional codes.

symptoms: Check engine light, decreased performance, possible smell of sulfur
likely_causes: Failed catalytic converter, damaged oxygen sensor, exhaust leak
diagnostic_steps: 1. Confirm P0420 code. 2. Perform O2 sensor voltage test pre- and post-cat. 3. Inspect exhaust for leaks. 4. Conduct catalyst temperature test. 5. Replace cat if temperature delta is low.

issue_name: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Large Leak)
symptoms: Check engine light, fuel odor after refuel
likely_causes: Loose or cracked fuel vapor hose, faulty EVAP purge valve, loose gas cap
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0455. 2. Inspect all EVAP hoses for cracks. 3. Tighten or replace loose connections. 4. Test purge valve operation. 5. Verify gas cap seal.

symptoms: Gear shifts feel sluggish, delayed response when accelerating
likely_causes: Low transmission fluid, worn clutch plates, TCM software glitch
diagnostic_steps: 1. Check transmission fluid level and condition. 2. Scan for any transmission-related codes. 3. Perform road test to note shift delays. 4. If fluid is ok, update TCM software. 5. If issue persists, have clutch pack inspected.

symptoms: Vibration in pedal during braking, noise
likely_causes: Warped brake rotors, uneven pad wear
diagnostic_steps: 1. Visual inspection of rotor surface for scoring or warping. 2. Measure rotor runout with dial indicator. 3. Check brake pad thickness. 4. Replace or resurface rotors if out of spec. 5. Bed new pads.

symptoms: Dim lights, engine stalls after shutdown, battery warning light
likely_causes: Faulty alternator diode, parasitic draw from accessory module, aged battery
diagnostic_steps: 1. Perform a parasitic draw test with multimeter (amps after 30 min). 2. Check alternator output voltage at idle and rev. 3. Inspect battery health with load tester. 4. Isolate circuits by pulling fuses to locate draw. 5. Repair or replace offending component.

symptoms: Tires wearing faster on inner side, pulling to one side
likely_causes: Worn control arm bushings, misaligned wheels
diagnostic_steps: 1. Inspect control arm bushings for cracks or play. 2. Perform wheel alignment check. 3. Replace any worn bushings. 4. Align wheels to factory specs. 5. Recheck tire wear after a short drive.

symptoms: Temperature gauge rising, coolant puddle under vehicle, steam
likely_causes: Cracked radiator hose, loose hose clamp, failed radiator
diagnostic_steps: 1. Inspect all coolant hoses for cracks or bulges. 2. Tighten or replace any loose clamps. 3. Pressure test cooling system for leaks. 4. Replace damaged hose or radiator as needed. 5. Refill coolant and bleed system.

symptoms: Check engine light, erratic electrical behavior
likely_causes: Weak battery, faulty voltage sensor, corroded battery terminals
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P0562 code. 2. Measure battery voltage with multimeter (should be ~12.6V resting). 3. Clean and tighten battery terminals. 4. Test voltage sensor output. 5. Replace battery or sensor if out of spec.

symptoms: Check engine light, rough idle, reduced fuel efficiency
likely_causes: Vacuum leak, clogged fuel filter, faulty MAF sensor
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for code P0171. 2. Inspect vacuum hoses for leaks. 3. Check MAF sensor voltage. 4. Measure fuel pressure. 5. Perform fuel trim analysis.

symptoms: Engine hesitation, loss of power, increased emissions
likely_causes: Worn spark plugs, faulty ignition coils, low fuel pressure
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve code P0300. 2. Conduct spark plug inspection and replace if needed. 3. Test ignition coil resistance. 4. Verify fuel pressure at rail.

issue_name: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Small Leak)
symptoms: Check engine light, faint fuel odor after fueling
likely_causes: Loose gas cap, cracked EVAP hose, faulty purge valve
diagnostic_steps: 1. Confirm code P0455. 2. Tighten or replace gas cap. 3. Perform smoke test on EVAP lines. 4. Test purge valve operation.

symptoms: Check engine light, reduced performance, higher emissions
likely_causes: Aged catalytic converter, oxygen sensor failure, exhaust leaks
diagnostic_steps: 1. Verify code P0420. 2. Inspect downstream O2 sensor voltage. 3. Check for exhaust leaks before converter. 4. Perform temperature sweep across converter.

symptoms: Gear shift delay, transmission warning lamp, erratic shifting
likely_causes: Faulty TCM, wiring issues, low transmission fluid
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0700 and any stored sub‑codes. 2. Check transmission fluid level and condition. 3. Inspect TCM connectors and wiring. 4. Perform TCM reflash if available.

symptoms: Hybrid system warning, reduced electric assist, possible limp mode
likely_causes: Faulty temperature sensor, degraded battery cells, wiring short
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve code P0A80. 2. Measure sensor resistance at specified temperature points. 3. Scan battery module health. 4. Inspect sensor harness for damage.

symptoms: Brake pedal drag, uneven brake pad wear, pulling to one side
likely_causes: Corroded piston pins, contaminated brake fluid
diagnostic_steps: 1. Inspect caliper movement by removing wheel. 2. Check for brake fluid leakage. 3. Test piston retraction with brake fluid pressure. 4. Replace or rebuild caliper if stuck.

symptoms: Clunking noise over bumps, loose steering feel
likely_causes: Age, high mileage, harsh road conditions
diagnostic_steps: 1. Perform bounce test on front corners. 2. Visually inspect bushings for cracks or deformation. 3. Check for excessive play in control arms.

symptoms: Engine runs hot after stop, fan does not engage on AC
likely_causes: Burnt relay contacts, corroded connector
diagnostic_steps: 1. Test fan operation with direct 12V supply. 2. Listen for relay click when AC is turned on. 3. Measure relay coil resistance. 4. Replace relay if faulty.

symptoms: Window does not move or moves intermittently, no related DTC
likely_causes: Worn contacts, moisture ingress
diagnostic_steps: 1. Check voltage at switch terminals while operating switch. 2. Test continuity through switch contacts. 3. Replace switch if voltage absent or intermittent.

symptoms: Check engine light, rough idle, poor acceleration
likely_causes: Vacuum leak, dirty mass airflow sensor, weak fuel pump
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for codes and verify P0171. 2. Inspect all vacuum hoses for cracks. 3. Clean MAF sensor with appropriate cleaner. 4. Measure fuel pressure; replace pump if below spec.

symptoms: Engine shake, loss of power, fuel smell
likely_causes: Faulty spark plugs, worn ignition coils, low fuel pressure
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P0300 code. 2. Perform spark plug visual inspection and replace if worn. 3. Test coil resistance per service manual. 4. Check fuel pressure with gauge.

symptoms: Check engine light, reduced fuel economy
likely_causes: Failing catalyst, upstream O2 sensor fault, exhaust leak
diagnostic_steps: 1. Verify P0420 code. 2. Scan O2 sensor data; compare upstream vs downstream readings. 3. Inspect exhaust manifold for leaks. 4. Perform temperature test across converter.

issue_name: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Large Leak)
symptoms: Check engine light, fuel smell after fueling
likely_causes: Loose gas cap, cracked EVAP hose, faulty canister vent valve
diagnostic_steps: 1. Confirm P0455 code. 2. Tighten or replace gas cap. 3. Perform smoke test on EVAP lines. 4. Replace vent valve if leak persists.

symptoms: Shift delays, transmission warning light
likely_causes: Faulty TCM, wiring issues, internal transmission fault
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0700 and related codes. 2. Check TCM power and ground circuits. 3. Use a multimeter to verify wiring continuity. 4. If wiring is good, replace TCM.

symptoms: Engine coolant temperature low, heater not warming
likely_causes: Stuck open thermostat, low coolant level
diagnostic_steps: 1. Verify P0128 code. 2. Measure coolant temperature with scan tool; compare to ambient. 3. Remove thermostat and test in hot water for opening temperature. 4. Replace if out of spec.

symptoms: Stalling, dim lights, no start
likely_causes: Weak battery, alternator failure, corroded connections
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0562. 2. Perform battery load test. 3. Measure alternator output at idle and 2500 rpm. 4. Clean and tighten battery terminals.

symptoms: Erratic speedometer, cruise control issues
likely_causes: Failed VSS, damaged wiring, connector corrosion
diagnostic_steps: 1. Confirm P0500 code. 2. Use multimeter to check VSS resistance while rotating wheel. 3. Inspect wiring harness for damage. 4. Replace VSS if out of range.

symptoms: Vibration through pedal during braking
likely_causes: Warped rotors, uneven pad wear
diagnostic_steps: 1. Jack up each wheel and spin to check for wobble. 2. Measure rotor runout with dial indicator. 3. Inspect pads for uneven wear. 4. Resurface or replace rotors and pads as needed.

issue_name: Steering Wheel Vibration at High Speed
symptoms: Vibration felt in steering wheel above 60 mph
likely_causes: Unbalanced tires, worn tie rod ends
diagnostic_steps: 1. Perform tire balance on all four wheels. 2. Inspect tie rod ends for looseness. 3. Check wheel alignment. 4. Rebalance or replace components as needed.

symptoms: Check engine light, rough idle, reduced fuel efficiency
likely_causes: Vacuum leak, clogged fuel filter, weak fuel pump
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for code P0171. 2. Inspect vacuum hoses for cracks. 3. Check fuel pressure with gauge. 4. Examine MAF sensor cleanliness. 5. Perform fuel trim reading.

symptoms: Engine shake, loss of power, increased emissions
likely_causes: Worn spark plugs, faulty ignition coils, low fuel pressure
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve code P0300. 2. Perform cylinder balance test. 3. Inspect spark plugs and replace if needed. 4. Test ignition coils resistance. 5. Check fuel pressure.

symptoms: Check engine light, reduced fuel economy, failed emissions test
likely_causes: Damaged catalyst, exhaust leak before sensor, faulty oxygen sensor
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0420. 2. Inspect exhaust manifold for leaks. 3. Test downstream O2 sensor voltage. 4. Perform catalyst temperature test. 5. Visual inspection of converter.

issue_name: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Large Leak)
symptoms: Check engine light, fuel odor, failed emissions
likely_causes: Loose gas cap, cracked EVAP hose, faulty purge valve
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P0455. 2. Verify gas cap is tightened. 3. Perform smoke test on EVAP lines. 4. Test purge valve operation with multimeter. 5. Inspect canister for damage.

symptoms: Delayed gear engagement, transmission warning light, erratic shifting
likely_causes: Faulty TCM, wiring issues, low transmission fluid
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0700 and related codes. 2. Check transmission fluid level and condition. 3. Inspect TCM connector pins for corrosion. 4. Perform TCM voltage test. 5. Consider TCM reflash or replacement.

symptoms: Brake pedal pulsation, uneven brake wear, pulling to one side
likely_causes: Corroded piston pin, contaminated brake fluid, seized slide pins
diagnostic_steps: 1. Inspect caliper for movement. 2. Remove caliper and check piston retraction. 3. Examine brake fluid for moisture. 4. Test brake pedal feel. 5. Replace or rebuild caliper as needed.

symptoms: Clunking noise over bumps, steering wheel vibration, uneven tire wear
likely_causes: Age, exposure to road salt, high mileage
diagnostic_steps: 1. Jack up front wheels and support vehicle. 2. Visually inspect bushings for cracks or deformation. 3. Apply force to control arm to detect play. 4. Listen for squeaks during bounce test. 5. Replace bushings if worn.

symptoms: Check engine light, poor idle, reduced fuel efficiency
likely_causes: Faulty sensor, wiring short, corroded connector
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0115. 2. Measure sensor resistance at cold and hot states. 3. Inspect wiring harness for damage. 4. Verify sensor voltage signal with live data. 5. Replace sensor if out of spec.

symptoms: Window sticks, clicks without movement, occasional operation loss
likely_causes: Worn contacts, moisture ingress, loose connector
diagnostic_steps: 1. Test window switch continuity with multimeter. 2. Wiggle switch while operating to detect intermittent loss. 3. Check wiring harness for corrosion. 4. Replace switch if faulty.

symptoms: Engine runs cool, longer warm-up time, increased emissions
likely_causes: Thermostat failed open, low coolant level
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0128. 2. Verify coolant temperature with gauge. 3. Remove thermostat and test in hot water for opening temperature. 4. Replace thermostat if it opens below spec. 5. Refill coolant to proper level.

issue_name: Mass Air Flow Sensor Circuit Malfunction
symptoms: Check engine light, rough idle, reduced acceleration
likely_causes: Dirty MAF sensor, cracked intake hose, electrical connector corrosion
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for DTC and verify P0101. 2. Inspect intake tubing for cracks or leaks. 3. Disconnect MAF sensor and measure voltage reference (5V). 4. Test sensor output voltage while engine runs (0.5-4.5V). 5. Clean MAF sensor with MAF cleaner if dirty. 6. Replace sensor if output remains out of range.

symptoms: Check engine light, increased fuel consumption, occasional knocking
likely_causes: Carbon buildup in EGR passages, stuck EGR valve, vacuum line leak
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve DTC P0401. 2. Locate EGR valve and inspect for carbon deposits. 3. Perform a vacuum test on the EGR control line. 4. Use a scan tool to command EGR open and observe change in idle speed. 5. Clean EGR passages and valve. 6. Replace valve if still faulty.

symptoms: Transmission warning light, erratic shifting, gear slippage
likely_causes: TCM software glitch, wiring harness damage, internal TCM failure
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0700 and any secondary codes. 2. Check TCM power and ground circuits for proper voltage. 3. Inspect wiring harness for chafing or corrosion. 4. Perform a transmission fluid level and condition check. 5. Reflash or update TCM software if available. 6. Replace TCM if diagnostics confirm failure.

symptoms: Check engine light, dimming headlights, difficulty starting
likely_causes: Weak battery, faulty alternator, corroded battery terminals
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0562. 2. Measure battery voltage with engine off (should be >12.4V). 3. Start engine and measure voltage (should rise to 13.5-14.5V). 4. Inspect battery terminals for corrosion and tighten connections. 5. Perform load test on battery. 6. Test alternator output; replace battery or alternator as needed.

issue_name: Torque Converter Clutch Performance or Stall Speed Too Low
symptoms: Transmission warning light, shuddering during acceleration, poor fuel economy
likely_causes: Clogged transmission fluid, faulty TCC solenoid, low fluid level
diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve P0720 and related codes. 2. Check transmission fluid level and condition; replace if burnt. 3. Test TCC solenoid resistance with multimeter (spec ~ 100-200 ohms). 4. Apply 12V to solenoid terminal to see if clutch engages. 5. Replace solenoid if out of spec. 6. Perform road test to verify resolution.

issue_name: Engine Speed Input Circuit No Signal
symptoms: Transmission fails to shift, no gear changes, engine may stall
likely_causes: Faulty crankshaft position sensor, damaged wiring, ECM failure
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0815. 2. Locate crankshaft position sensor and inspect connector. 3. Measure sensor signal voltage while cranking (should see 0-5V pulses). 4. Check wiring continuity to ECM. 5. Replace sensor if no signal. 6. If sensor is good, test ECM input circuit.

symptoms: Hard brake pedal, longer stopping distance, hissing sound
likely_causes: Cracked brake booster diaphragm, loose vacuum hose, failed check valve
diagnostic_steps: 1. Inspect vacuum hose from engine to booster for cracks or disconnections. 2. Listen for hissing while pressing brake pedal. 3. Perform a vacuum test on booster using a hand pump; pressure should hold. 4. Check brake booster mounting for damage. 5. Replace booster or hose as necessary.

issue_name: Power Steering Fluid Leak from Rack
symptoms: Whining noise when steering, fluid puddles under vehicle, stiff steering
likely_causes: Worn rack seals, damaged hose, cracked rack housing
diagnostic_steps: 1. Examine ground under vehicle for power steering fluid. 2. Inspect rack seals and boots for leakage. 3. Check power steering lines for cracks. 4. Replace leaking seals or rack assembly. 5. Refill system with correct fluid and bleed air.

issue_name: Radiator Coolant Temperature Sensor Stuck Open
symptoms: Check engine light, poor fuel economy, engine runs rich
likely_causes: Sensor wiring short, sensor internal failure
diagnostic_steps: 1. Locate coolant temperature sensor and disconnect connector. 2. Measure resistance; should change with temperature. 3. Compare reading to service specs. 4. Replace sensor if resistance is constant or out of range. 5. Clear DTCs and test drive.

issue_name: Front Left Suspension Shock Absorber Leak
symptoms: Uneven ride height, noticeable wobble over bumps, fluid drips
likely_causes: Damaged shock seal, worn internal components
diagnostic_steps: 1. Inspect shock absorber for oil leakage or damage. 2. Push down on front left corner; observe rebound speed. 3. Compare ride height to opposite side. 4. Replace shock absorber if leak or poor damping observed. 5. Re-torque mounting bolts to spec.
